public_rationale: The Stanford AI Index 2025 shows the antecedent: many developers now offer comparable high-quality models. Price wars followed. In May 2024, ByteDance priced its Doubao Pro LLM about 99% below the industry average. Alibaba responded with cuts of up to 97%, and Baidu made some models free. Reports framed this as a competitive price war. That fits the plain reading: comparable models lead rivals to compete on price. One caveat: Epoch AI found no clear evidence that shrinking margins drove the global fall in LLM prices. Some of the decline likely reflects lower costs, not price wars alone.
limitations: The clearest documented price war is in China (2024). Global price declines may be partly cost-driven.
The causal link is inferred from timing and how the reports frame the cuts, not tested.

criteria.support_condition: Documented rounds of competitive LLM price cuts, with credible sources attributing them to competition among rivals offering comparable models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No competitive price cutting occurred, or credible analysis shows price falls were driven only by lower costs, with no competitive undercutting.

evidence.excerpt:
ByteDance revealed the slashed price for its Doubao Pro LLM, at 0.0008 yuan per 1,000 tokens, which is reportedly 99% lower than the industry average for enterprise users.

In response, Alibaba’s cloud unit announced up to 97% price cuts on a range of its Tongyi Qwen LLMs.
evidence.explanation: Documents a tit-for-tat round of steep LLM price cuts among rival providers, which the article frames as fighting off competition. This is a price war in the plain sense.
